intended_object: The canonical map ι_i : M_i → colim_j M_j into the directed colimit of a directed system of modules M_j over a directed system of (commutative) semirings A_j. It sends m to the class of (i, m) and is semilinear along the canonical ring map A_i → colim_j A_j. This is inferred from the docstring and from how the file uses it.
explanation:
The definition sends m to ⟦⟨i, m⟩⟧ in the concrete `DirectLimit M g`. This is the standard insertion of the i-th stage into the colimit. It is additive by `DirectLimit.add_def`. It is semilinear along `DirectLimit.Ring.of A f i : A i →+* DirectLimit A f`, because the file defines the action of the scalar limit on the module limit stagewise (`smul_mk`: ⟦(i,a)⟧ • ⟦(i,m)⟧ = ⟦(i, a•m)⟧). This is exactly the textbook property of the canonical map into a colimit of modules over a colimit of rings.

Mathlib has only fixed-scalar versions: `DirectLimit.Module.of`, which is R-linear for a single semiring R, and `Module.DirectLimit.of`. It has no varying-scalar version, so this definition is not a duplicate of an existing construction.

The setting is the natural one:
- Directedness and nonemptiness of ι are needed for the concrete direct-limit structure.
- The semilinear system g along f is exactly the data of a module system over a ring system.
- Commutativity of the A_i is slightly more than the module structure alone needs. It is the natural setting for this file, whose purpose is the tensor-product comparison. This is not a meaningful narrowing.
